take_homes: The AI fills gaps with what people like me usually say, and it grades its own work too kindly, so I check its account against what I know.
Changing what the agent is given changes what comes out, and a plain rules file can carry that over to the next session.
A second reader with no history is a cheap test I can run myself.

monday.move: Run the cold-critic step on one real document of mine (a board memo), and compare its 'generic' picks with my own gut.
monday.when: Tuesday, one slot between steering groups, if it fits
monday.stop_condition: If it takes more than 30 minutes or the output is just flattery, I drop it.
monday.blocker: The calendar, and not being sure what I'm allowed to paste into the tool.

misconception.why: They said what the tool gets wrong, and I could test it on my own profile. That's not the agile pitch. The repeated filler notes pulled the other way and almost undid it, and I still can't tell whether this blows over.

one_line: There's one honest hour in it, the part where it admits the tool flatters itself, buried under the same management paragraph pasted in twelve times.
